html:
The Dau Nom Wintu are one of the bands of the Wintu, a Native people of the upper Sacramento River valley in northern California. This territory lies west and south of present Redding.

The Wintu spoke a Wintuan language and lived in villages along the rivers, fishing for salmon and gathering acorns. The California Gold Rush brought miners into their valleys after 1849, and massacres, disease and forced removal followed. Shasta Dam, finished in 1945, flooded many of their village and burial sites. Other Wintu bands on the map include the Nom Ti Pom and the northern Wintu.
